NDT training in Portsmouth, NH: how it works on the Seacoast

Short answer: If you work or want to work around Portsmouth, you can take NDT theory online at your own pace with Atlantis and an ASNT Level III available for questions, then do practical work in the Practical NDT simulator and in person at an employer's own facility. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Portsmouth. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies you. We reply within one business day.

Portsmouth is small but has a surprisingly dense technical economy. Across the river in Kittery, Maine, Portsmouth Naval Shipyard overhauls and modernises Navy submarines. Behind the shipyard sits a regional supplier base that machines, welds, tests and ships parts to naval standards. Further down the coast is the Seabrook nuclear station, and just inland the Pease Tradeport hosts aviation and technology employers.

That variety shapes what people search for. Some want "ndt training Portsmouth NH" because they have a welding or machining background and see inspection as the next step. Some are veterans who worked on submarines or aircraft. Others are quality managers at small suppliers who have just learned that a prime contractor wants proof of qualification.

The sections below set out the certification steps, the methods in demand, how to compare schools, and what employers can do to train a crew near the Seacoast. For the state view see NDT training in New Hampshire; for the national view see NDT training in the USA and our training overview.

How to get NDT certified in Portsmouth: the SNT-TC-1A route

  1. Start with the employer's rulebook. A written practice defines what training, experience and testing each level requires. Ask to see it, or ask what it requires before you apply.
  2. Get the classroom hours done. Online theory can fill the formal training portion. The training-requirements matrix shows common recommended hours.
  3. Work under a certified person. Experience hours are recorded and signed by a Level II or III who supervised you.
  4. Pass the general examination. It tests the principles and equipment of the method.
  5. Pass the specific examination. It tests the employer's procedures and acceptance criteria. For Navy suppliers those criteria often arrive through purchase order flow-down.
  6. Complete the practical. You operate the equipment on specimens while a grader assesses your technique and your findings.
  7. Maintain your vision record. Tests are repeated at the interval set by the written practice.
  8. Receive the certificate from your employer and recertify on the schedule the document sets.

Use the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker to see where your current hours put you.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Seacoast technicians

MethodWhat the course coversWhere it is used around Portsmouth
VTWeld and surface inspection, lighting, gauging, written recordsShipyard suppliers, boat builders, fabricators, bridge and port structures
PTSurface preparation, penetrant processing, evaluationStainless and non-magnetic marine piping, aerospace and precision parts
MTMagnetisation, particle selection, field checksFerritic welds, forgings, fittings and structural steel
UTCalibration, thickness, straight-beam and angle-beam weld workPlate and weld examination for marine and industrial fabricators, thickness gauging
RTExposure, image quality, film and digital interpretationPiping welds and castings; radiation safety licensed by the state
ETImpedance-plane theory, probes, calibrationAviation components, tubing and conductive-material surface work

Level I trains people to work under direction. Level II teaches calibration, interpretation and evaluation against codes. Level III preparation covers the ASNT Basic and Method examinations and procedure writing. Read more on the Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 pages.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training near Portsmouth

For fabricated steel and thick-section welds, UT is the method that sees inside the material. Marine structures, pressure piping and heavy weldments around the Seacoast depend on it for thickness checks, plate quality and weld volume.

The UT course teaches how sound travels and reflects, how to set up and calibrate an instrument, and how to scan welds with enough coverage to trust the result. Candidates also practise reporting: where the indication is, how large it appears, and how it compares with the acceptance limit.

Work through the UT Level 2 practice questions and the practice test library to find weak spots.

Where NDT technicians work around Portsmouth

Naval shipyard and supply chain. Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, in Kittery, Maine, overhauls, repairs and modernises Navy submarines. The yard qualifies its own workforce. The broader opportunity is among the contractors and suppliers that support naval work throughout New England and have to meet NAVSEA requirements flowed down in contracts. Those requirements are the employer's responsibility; Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based background rather than a substitute for them.

Nuclear power. NextEra Energy's Seabrook Station is a nuclear generating plant on the New Hampshire coast. Outage work follows ASME Section XI and plant quality assurance rules, and contractors are qualified by the site.

Aviation and technology. The Pease International Tradeport hosts the New Hampshire Air National Guard and a cluster of aviation, manufacturing and technology firms, creating demand for aerospace-style VT, PT and ET.

Port and bridges. The working port on the Piscataqua and the bridges linking New Hampshire and Maine need structural inspection, with bridge welding typically to AWS D1.5.

Boatbuilding and fabrication. Seacoast shipwrights, machine shops and small fabricators need VT, PT and MT on welds and machined parts, and some require UT or RT.

For pay information from public sources, see the NDT salary guide.

NDT schools and classes near Portsmouth: how to compare

A search for "ndt school near me" on the Seacoast produces a few in-person programmes and several online ones. They suit different people.

  • In-person programmes suit people who want an instructor in the room and can travel. Check whether the programme leads to something employers here accept.
  • Online theory suits shift workers and people with long commutes. It is theory only.
  • Employer-site practicals put the hands-on work on the equipment you will use at work.

Ask every provider the same questions. Which certification scheme does the training support? Who grades the practical? What records will you receive? Is the instructor certified in the methods taught? How are retakes handled? A provider that implies certification without an employer's written practice is describing a different scheme from SNT-TC-1A.

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Portsmouth. We offer online theory, a simulator and employer-site practicals led by an ASNT Level III. If a local programme fits your life better, take it and bring the records to your employer.

Online NDT training in New Hampshire

From anywhere in New Hampshire you can study NDT theory online, starting the moment you enrol. The courses run year-round, and an ASNT Level III answers questions as you work through them. This is how many Seacoast technicians study around shifts at the shipyard, the plant or a boatyard.

Online learning covers the formal classroom hours only. Experience and the practical examination happen hands-on. The online training page and FAQ explain how the parts fit together. Add time in the Practical NDT simulator to practise setups before the practical.

Training a crew at your Seacoast facility

Suppliers in the naval and aviation chains often have to qualify several people at once and keep immaculate records. We can review your written practice against the requirements your customers impose, give each trainee theory access, and run the specific and practical examinations at your site on your own procedures and parts, under Level III oversight.

  • Written practice authoring or revision: details.
  • Examination preparation and grading.
  • Pre-audit review of qualification files.
  • Outside Level III coverage: Level III consulting.

Read about corporate NDT training or ask about training for your Portsmouth-area team.

Radiography licensing in New Hampshire and Maine

Radiography has a legal layer that other methods lack. New Hampshire is an NRC Agreement State, and the Department of Health and Human Services' radiological health programme regulates radiation sources there. Across the river, Maine has its own programme. Companies need the right licence or registration in each state where they work, and radiographers must meet that state's training requirements.

An RT course under SNT-TC-1A teaches technique and interpretation but does not authorise anyone to use a source. Seacoast crews that cross the bridge between states should confirm reciprocity before mobilising. Check current rules with the relevant agency.

What small suppliers on the Seacoast should do first

If you run quality at a small firm that supplies the shipyard, a boat builder or an aerospace customer, resist the urge to start by buying courses. Begin by reading the purchase order and the specifications that came with it. Make a list of every method and technique named, then compare it with your written practice. Gaps usually show up in two places: methods you use but never wrote down, and techniques the customer specifies that nobody on your staff has been examined on.

Then look at your people. For each technician, list the methods, the level, the last examination and the date the vision record expires. Anyone with a lapse needs attention before the next audit. Only then choose training to close the gaps. This sequence saves money because it replaces blanket courses with targeted ones, and it gives a Level III a clear brief when you ask for help.

Veterans and career changers on the Seacoast

The Portsmouth area has many people who learned technical skills in the Navy or Air National Guard and now want a civilian trade. Military maintenance experience is valuable, but it does not automatically count toward civilian NDT experience hours. Whether it counts is decided by the employer's written practice and its Level III, who will look at what you actually did and under what supervision. Bring records, not just job titles.

Career changers from welding, machining or electronics start from a different place. A welder already understands joint geometry and discontinuities, which is a head start in VT and MT. A machinist knows tolerances and surface finish, which helps with PT and ET. Someone from electronics may find UT instruments and eddy current electronics natural. Whatever your background, the route is the same: theory, supervised experience, examination, employer certification. What changes is which method you can learn fastest and which employer will value you most.

If you are unsure how your history maps to a level, run it through the eligibility checker and then ask a prospective employer's Level III to confirm. That conversation is also a good way to learn what the employer wants to see on your resume before an interview.

Practise before your practical exam

The Practical NDT simulator lets you rehearse calibration, scan plans and interpretation in virtual workplaces. It supplements, but does not replace, real-specimen practicals and logged experience. Test recall with the practice tests. The instructor is Anoop Rayavarapu, who holds ASNT NDT Level III certification in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT and has worked internationally in the field for over eleven years.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Portsmouth

How do I get into NDT near Portsmouth, NH?

Study theory online, then look for shipyard suppliers, fabricators and aviation firms that hire and certify trainees.

Are there NDT classes near me on the Seacoast?

A few in-person options exist. Atlantis offers online theory and an employer-site practical, with no Portsmouth classroom.

Will your course let me work inside the naval shipyard?

No outside course does that alone. The yard qualifies its own people; suppliers certify under their own programmes.

Does a course give me certification?

No. Under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you.

How much is NDT training?

The published US fees on this page cover standard courses; for group or custom work, contact us for a reply within one business day.

Which method should I learn first?

VT, then PT or MT. UT follows as you gain experience.

Can I study online in New Hampshire?

Yes. Theory is online and self-paced; practicals are in person.

Are there NDT jobs near Portsmouth?

Yes, among naval suppliers, aviation firms, boatyards, bridge work and the nuclear station's contractors.

Do I need a Maine licence to X-ray in Kittery?

Radiography across the river falls under Maine's rules. Check with the state before working there.

Can you train our team at our shop?

Yes. Compare Boston, Bath and Providence, or contact us.
